lessons.title: Be careful!
lessons.kind: 对话课本剧 · 装饰美术教室时 Danny 爬椅子挂星星摔下来
canonical: The students are decorating the art classroom.
Look at this yellow star, Brian and Jenny! Isn’t it beautiful? I’m going to hang it from the ceiling over the desk.
Here is the tape. I’ll get the ladder for you.
I don’t need a ladder. I think I’m tall enough.
Danny can’t reach the ceiling, so he climbs onto Mr Green’s chair.
Almost… Almost… Aaaaaaahhhh!
Danny falls.
What was that noise?!
He sees Danny lying on the floor.
Danny, are you okay? Are you hurt?
Hmm… My tail is a little sore, but it’s not serious.
Then, they hear Brian cry for help, but his voice is very weak.
Brian? Where are you?
Help me, sir! I’m under Danny!
Oh no! I’m really sorry! Are you okay, Brian?
No, I’m opposite of okay. I tried to catch you, but you landed on top of me. My arm hurts.
Should I call an ambulance?
No, that’s not necessary. I don’t think my arm is broken.
Jenny, please call Brian’s mother. Tell her we are taking Brian to the hospital. He should get an X-ray just in case.

lessons.title: Safety education
lessons.kind: 日记 · Li Ming 记录全国安全教育日的消防演练与急救学习
canonical: Today is National Safety Education Day. Our school organised activities to teach us about safety.
The first part was fire safety. What should people do in case of a fire emergency? A firefighter gave us a talk and showed us videos.
He said that if there is a fire, we should stay calm, find the nearest exit to go outside, and never use lifts.
We even had a fire drill! As soon as the fire alarm rang, all the students took action. We covered our mouths and noses with wet towels.
We walked down the stairs calmly and in order. Our teachers guided us outside.
After the drill, the firefighter taught us how to put out a fire with water or with a fire extinguisher. We did it!
Later, we learned some first aid skills, like CPR and other basic life support training. We talked about online safety practices and where to find help in any emergency.
We discussed how to stay safe in a big crowd, and what to do to avoid drowning.
The safety education activities helped us understand how to stay safe and make good choices in different situations.

lessons.title: My helmet saved my life!
lessons.kind: 记叙文 · 女孩骑车摔倒，头盔替她挡下尖石
canonical: It was a beautiful noon. I was riding my bicycle by the river, thinking about yesterday’s baseball game. I guess I rode over a hole in the road. All of a sudden, WHAM!
I went down hard on my right side. That really hurt!
My head hit the ground. I lay there for a few minutes. I tried to get up, but I couldn’t! “There’s something wrong with me,” I thought.
I felt so terrible that I lay down again. Then I saw blood on my shoe. My hand and knee were bleeding. I was in a lot of pain.
As I lay there, I took off my helmet. There was a sharp rock sticking out of it. It was pretty scary to look at. Thank goodness I wore my helmet! I shouted for help.
A driver stopped his truck and came to help me. He put my bike in the back of his truck and drove me to the hospital.
When my mother got to the hospital, she gave me a big hug and kiss. “You were wearing your helmet this time. How lucky you were!” she said.
She knew I was careless and did not always wear my helmet.
But I’ll never be careless again... My bicycle helmet saved my life!

lessons.title: An accident on the street
lessons.kind: 新闻报道 · 13 岁女孩过街追球被车撞伤
canonical: NORTH TOWN, Alberta. Thirteen-year-old Ann Brown was hit by a car outside North Town Primary School at 15 Park Road. The accident happened at about 7:30 a.m.
She and her brother, James, were on their way to an early basketball practice.
“We were in a hurry,” James told the reporter. “We didn’t want to be late for practice. Ann’s basketball rolled onto the street. She raced to get it.”
Mrs Andrews, a chemistry teacher from Green Wood School, was walking several steps behind the two students. She saw it happen.
“I don’t know whose fault it was,” Mrs Andrews said. “The girl didn’t see the car. And the street was icy — the car couldn’t stop in time. It was terrible.”
Mrs Andrews said, “I shouted to the girl. I wanted to stop her from running after the ball, but she didn’t hear me.”
After the accident, the car stopped, and the driver, Bill Morin, jumped out. He called an ambulance.
Mr Morin knows first aid. He did not move Ann. He stopped traffic on the road until the ambulance came. Then the ambulance took both students to the hospital.
Both kids were in shock.
Ann has a broken leg and a bad shoulder wound. She is recovering in the hospital. Doctors say she can expect to return to school in about a week.

lessons.title: Home safety
lessons.kind: 说明文 · 厨房与浴室的居家安全提示
canonical: Many serious accidents happen in people’s homes. The kitchen and the bathroom are the two most dangerous places in the house.
Can people prevent certain accidents? Yes. Many accidents happen because people are careless. So be careful!
Be careful with fire and boiling water when you cook.
Have fire blankets, fire extinguishers, smoke alarms, and flashlights near the kitchen.
Always turn off the oven or stove after use. In case of a gas leak, do not use a cell phone or any electric item.
Immediately turn off the stove and quickly open a window. Move to a safe area to inform emergency services and the gas company.
Never use electricity in the shower or bathtub. It can shock you!
Be sure to keep the bathroom floor dry after you take a shower or bath. It’s easy to slip and fall on a wet floor.
Turn on the cold water first when taking a bath. Then adjust the hot water to ensure a safe water temperature. Hot water can burn you.
Home safety focuses on preventing accidents and reacting well to dangers in order to protect the safety of the family.

lessons.title: Being cybersafe
lessons.kind: 说明文 · 个人信息、虚假信息与网络欺凌
canonical: Technology can be good or bad. That’s why learning to be cybersafe is so important! Never give out private information online. Question the information you read.
Most of us have our names and photos on social media. But without the right privacy settings, they can be used by dangerous people.
Everything you post or send online could be taken and used against your will. And once it’s online, it’s nearly impossible to get rid of it completely!
Also be careful of what others send you. If you click a link or open an attachment, it can be something dangerous for your computer, like a virus.
The internet era makes gathering information easy. But you must consider the source of the information you are reading.
Who published it, a stranger or an expert in the field? What website is it on, a blog or a government resource? Does it offer different views?
Is it meant to inform you, or simply get a quick reaction?
You probably know that cyberbullying is bullying, but online.
Sending hurtful messages, spreading lies about someone, sharing their private photos... these are easy to do, but they have a huge impact on the victim.
The best way to deal with cyberbullying is to ignore, block, and delete. Telling a trusted adult is also important, especially if someone is threatening you.
Be kind to others. Be careful with your information. Think critically about everything you see online. This will ensure you are cybersafe!
